immosphere.title: ImmoSphere
immosphere.excerpt: Real-estate decision support on aggregated, multi-source data — PostGIS, self-hosted vector tiles, FastAPI microservices on AWS (immosphere.co).
immosphere.coverAlt: ImmoSphere project preview — real estate analytics platform
immosphere.sectionOverview:
**ImmoSphere** is a web application for real-estate decision support built on aggregated, **multi-source** property and market data.

The product helps users explore and compare geographic areas across multiple indicators (prices, yields, demographics, amenities, energy performance, and more) to inform investment and usage decisions, with **map-first** interactive exploration.

Co-built with a **wealth management advisor**: they lead domain framing and commercial development; I lead technical design, implementation, and operations.
immosphere.sectionKeywords: real estate, decision support, data analytics, multi-source data, interactive mapping, geospatial, microservices, data pipelines
immosphere.sectionFeatures:
End-to-end delivery of a decision-support product: data ingestion and transformation, REST APIs, **PostgreSQL/PostGIS**, React frontend, containerized deployment on **AWS** (EC2, RDS), and day-to-day production care.

Multi-indicator analysis (e.g. transactions, rents, DPE, equipment, population/housing) exposed through a **unified API** behind a gateway.
immosphere.sectionFeaturesList:
- National map layers: interactive coverage of **metropolitan France**—sales from 2014 onward, DPE from 2021, and price and neighborhood dynamics at multiple geographic scales.
- Property analyzer: from address, floor area, property type, and other inputs, **dashboards** summarize the home, its immediate context, and the neighborhood.
- Market explorer: explore a **local market** from a chosen **geographic zone**, with consolidated real-estate and **socio-demographic** statistics to understand how that market behaves.
immosphere.sectionStack:
- Deployment & infrastructure: AWS EC2, Dockerized services, Amazon RDS, Amazon Cognito for authentication, AWS Amplify for the frontend
- Architecture & backend: Python / FastAPI microservices behind a central API Gateway; service boundaries aligned with business areas; TileServer for maps
- Data layer: multi-source ingestion pipelines in Python; processing and loading into PostgreSQL/PostGIS or conversion to vector tiles
- Security: Cognito JWT (Amplify on the client); access via Cognito groups; Cloudflare
- Observability: structured logging (optional JSON), X-Correlation-ID propagation, PII sanitization, custom-built admin monitoring UI
- Frontend: React (Vite), React Router, Tailwind, MapLibre for maps
- Testing & CI: GitHub Actions (lint, backend and frontend tests), Docker Compose–based CI

secureops.title: SecureOps
secureops.excerpt: Cybersecurity application — OWASP Top 10 web scanner and microservices architecture (secureops.fr).
secureops.coverAlt: SecureOps project preview — web vulnerability scanner
secureops.sectionOverviewLead: **SecureOps** is a web security product for **OWASP Top 10–style checks** on target URLs.
secureops.sectionOverviewCiPrefix: On secureops.fr you can pull reports and schedule scans; in CI/CD, run the same checks with the
secureops.sectionOverviewStatus: What's live today: passive analysis and web crawlers. **Intrusive testing** is still in development.
secureops.sectionKeywords: cybersecurity, OWASP Top 10, vulnerability scanner, web security, microservices, custom queues, workers, orchestration, asynchronous processing
secureops.sectionFeatures:
Engineering of the **passive analysis pipeline**: HTTP/TLS and configuration signals, security headers, technology fingerprinting, and misconfiguration heuristics, correlated to **OWASP Top 10–style risk families**—without active exploitation in what’s exposed online today.

**Crawl jobs** map the reachable surface (link following, scoping rules) so scans can target a discovered set of URLs and assets instead of a **single entry point**.

**Asynchronous execution** end to end: FastAPI services accept scan/crawl requests and enqueue work in **PostgreSQL-backed queues**; dedicated workers poll, execute the engine, and write status and findings back—keeping APIs responsive, absorbing spikes, and isolating failures per job.
secureops.sectionStack:
- Deployment & infrastructure: AWS EC2, Dockerized services, PostgreSQL running on that EC2 instance, Amazon Cognito for authentication, AWS Amplify for the frontend
- Architecture & backend: FastAPI microservices behind an API Gateway; asynchronous scan execution via PostgreSQL-backed job queues and dedicated workers
- Data layer: PostgreSQL; scan results stored as JSON; indexed tables (status, retry, timestamps); on-demand PDF reports
- Security: Cognito JWT and API keys; basic RBAC; in-memory rate limiting; SSRF safeguards (private networks blocked, timeouts); Cloudflare for edge and application protection
- Observability: structured logging (optional JSON), X-Correlation-ID propagation, PII sanitization, custom-built admin monitoring UI
- Frontend: Next.js (App Router) and Tailwind; async job tracking via polling with backoff
- Testing & CI: GitHub Actions (lint, backend and frontend tests), Docker-based workflows
